title: Modulo 9 classification of prime pairs (p, p+g): an empirical verification of the Hardy-Littlewood conjecture for g = 18k
description: Source code, computational scripts and datasets accompanying the paper of the same title by Giovanni Ferraiuolo. Contents: LaTeX source and compiled PDF of the paper; Python scripts for prime sieving, pair counting, regression analysis, aggregate verification against OEIS A007508, and chi-square goodness-of-fit; CSV datasets of empirical counts up to x = 10^9 (twin primes by DR mod 9) and x = 5*10^7 (gap family g = 18k, k in {5,7,10,11,12,13,15,17,20}); high-resolution PDF figures (convergence, aggregate decay, equipartition, HL confirmation). The work tests Hardy-Littlewood in arithmetic progressions modulo 9 for prime pairs (p, p+g). Twin primes serve as a zero-calibration baseline: equidistribution across three admissible classes within +-0.025 percentage points at X = 10^9 (chi^2 = 0.82, df=2, p = 0.67), and aggregate count agreeing with 2*C_2*li_2(X) within |rho - 1| <= 3*10^-8 at X = 10^18 (via OEIS A007508 / Oliveira e Silva). The empirical decay follows an X^(-1/2) log X law with fitted slope -0.45 +- 0.03, in line with the function-field analogues of Sawin-Shusterman (Annals 2022) and Keating-Rudnick (IMRN 2014). The family g = 18k provides nine independent gap configurations spanning H(g) in [2.64, 3.52]: the singular series prediction is confirmed within +-0.15% at x = 5*10^7, and equidistribution across the six admissible residue classes mod 9 holds within +-0.14 percentage points at x = 10^7.
